robotics.serial_dof.title: Degrees of freedom of a serial open chain

variables.name: joints
variables.desc: joint types in order, e.g. ['R','R','P']; R/P=1, U/C=2, S=3 freedoms

assumptions: Serial (open) chain: the DoF is the sum of the joint freedoms. Closed-loop mobility is mechanisms.dof_planar / dof_spatial (Grübler/Kutzbach).
method_references: Mobility of a serial manipulator = Σ joint freedoms

robotics.planar_2r_workspace.title: Workspace of a planar 2-link arm
assumptions: Revolute joints with no joint limits; the reachable set is the annulus R_min ≤ r ≤ R_max. Area = π(R_max² − R_min²) = 4π L1 L2.
method_references: Annular workspace of a planar 2R arm

robotics.dh_forward.title: Denavit–Hartenberg forward kinematics

variables.name: T
variables.desc: 4x4 homogeneous transform of the tool frame

variables.name: pos
variables.desc: tool position [x, y, z] in m

variables.name: rot
variables.desc: 3x3 rotation matrix of the tool frame

assumptions: Standard DH: T = Rot_z(θ)Trans_z(d)Trans_x(a)Rot_x(α); modified (Craig): T = Rot_x(α)Trans_x(a)Rot_z(θ)Trans_z(d). Angles are given in degrees in the table.
The joint rows are fixed parameters or joint variables: substitute joint values for revolute θ or prismatic d.
method_references: Denavit–Hartenberg convention; product of link transforms

robotics.homogeneous_transform.title: Homogeneous transform from rotation and translation, with inverse

procedure.python:
def _homogeneous_transform(v):
    """Build a 4x4 homogeneous transform from a rotation matrix and translation, and its inverse."""
    p = v['translation']
    R = v['rotation']
    if not isinstance(p, (list, tuple)) or len(p) != 3:
        raise MechError('translation: give [x, y, z] in m')
    if not isinstance(R, (list, tuple)) or len(R) != 3 or any(len(row) != 3 for row in R):
        raise MechError('rotation: give a 3x3 rotation matrix')
    tx, ty, tz = (float(x) for x in p)
    R = [[float(x) for x in row] for row in R]
    Rn = np.array(R)
    if not np.allclose(Rn.T @ Rn, np.eye(3), atol=1e-6):
        raise MechError('rotation: R must be orthonormal (RᵀR = I); check that the columns are mutually '
                        'orthogonal unit vectors')
    if abs(float(np.linalg.det(Rn)) - 1.0) > 1e-6:
        raise MechError('rotation: det R must be +1 for a proper rotation (a reflection has det = −1)')
    T = [[R[0][0], R[0][1], R[0][2], tx],
         [R[1][0], R[1][1], R[1][2], ty],
         [R[2][0], R[2][1], R[2][2], tz],
         [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]]
    RT = [[R[j][i] for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]  # transpose
    q = [-sum(RT[i][j] * p[j] for j in range(3)) for i in range(3)]
    Ti = [[RT[0][0], RT[0][1], RT[0][2], q[0]],
          [RT[1][0], RT[1][1], RT[1][2], q[1]],
          [RT[2][0], RT[2][1], RT[2][2], q[2]],
          [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]]
    return {'T': T, 'T_inv': Ti}

assumptions: R must be a proper rotation matrix; the inverse of T = [R p; 0 1] is [Rᵀ −Rᵀp; 0 1].
method_references: Homogeneous representation of a rigid-body transform

robotics.planar_2r_ik.title: Inverse kinematics of a planar 2R arm (two elbow branches)

variables.name: elbow_a
variables.desc: [x, y] of the elbow, elbow-down branch

variables.name: elbow_b
variables.desc: [x, y] of the elbow, elbow-up branch

assumptions: Angles measured from +x, with θ2 relative to link 1. In the standard (Spong) sense the branch with θ2 = +acos(c2) places the elbow below the base–tip line (elbow down) and θ2 = −acos(c2) places it above (elbow up). Two solutions exist for every reachable point; at the workspace boundary they coincide. Unreachable targets raise an error.
method_references: Law of cosines and atan2 for the planar 2R inverse kinematics

robotics.planar_3r_ik.title: Inverse kinematics of a planar 3R arm (position and orientation)
assumptions: With a specified tip orientation φ the redundancy is removed: the wrist point is solved with the 2R formulas and θ3 = φ − θ1 − θ2.
method_references: Wrist-centring reduction of the planar 3R IK to a 2R problem

robotics.numeric_ik.title: Numeric inverse kinematics of a planar n-link arm (damped least squares)

variables.name: target
variables.desc: target tip position [x, y] in m

variables.name: position
variables.desc: reached tip position [x, y] in m

procedure.python:
def _numeric_ik(v):
    """Numeric IK of a general planar n-link arm by damped least squares (deterministic)."""
    links = v['links']
    guess = v['guess']
    target = v['target']
    if not isinstance(links, list) or not links or any(L <= 0 for L in links):
        raise MechError('links: give positive link lengths [L1, ...] in m')
    if not isinstance(guess, list) or len(guess) != len(links):
        raise MechError('guess: give one initial joint angle (rad) per link')
    if not isinstance(target, list) or len(target) != 2:
        raise MechError('target: give [x, y] in m')
    theta = np.array([float(t) for t in guess])
    x_t, y_t = float(target[0]), float(target[1])
    # Reachability pre-check: a planar n-link arm reaches exactly the annulus [R_min, R_max].
    r_t = math.hypot(x_t, y_t)
    r_max = sum(links)
    r_min = max(0.0, 2.0 * max(links) - r_max)
    if r_t > r_max + 1e-9 or r_t < r_min - 1e-9:
        raise MechError(f'target ({x_t}, {y_t}) is outside the workspace: reachable radius is '
                        f'{r_min:g} .. {r_max:g} m (target is at r = {r_t:g} m)')
    lam = 1e-3
    err = 0.0
    for _ in range(400):
        x, y = _fk_planar(links, theta)
        e = np.array([x_t - x, y_t - y])
        err = float(np.hypot(*e))
        if err < 1e-9:
            break
        J = _jacobian_planar(links, theta)
        JTJ = J @ J.T
        step = J.T @ np.linalg.solve(JTJ + lam * lam * np.eye(2), e)
        theta = theta + step
    theta = np.arctan2(np.sin(theta), np.cos(theta))  # wrap each angle to (−π, π]
    x, y = _fk_planar(links, theta)
    err = float(math.hypot(x_t - x, y_t - y))
    if err > 1e-6:
        raise MechError(f'numeric IK did not converge to the target ({x_t}, {y_t}) '
                        f'(final error {err:.3g} m after 400 iterations); the damped least-squares solver '
                        f'fell into a local minimum — try a different initial guess')
    return {'angles': [float(t) for t in theta], 'position': [x, y], 'error': err}

assumptions: Damped least squares (Levenberg) with 400 fixed iterations; converges to the local solution nearest the guess. Redundant arms yield the minimum-norm step direction. Deterministic (no random restarts).

robotics.planar_jacobian.title: Geometric Jacobian and joint velocities of a planar n-link arm

variables.name: det
variables.desc: det J (2R) or det(J·Jᵀ) for n>2

variables.name: residual
variables.desc: ‖J θ̇ − v‖: unachieved part of the requested tip velocity

procedure.python:
def _planar_jacobian(v):
    """Geometric Jacobian of a planar n-link arm and joint velocities for a given tip velocity.

    joint_vel is the minimum-norm (pseudo-inverse) solution of J θ̇ = v; `residual` reports how much of
    the requested tip velocity is actually achieved (‖J θ̇ − v‖), which is non-zero only at a singularity.
    """
    links = v['links']
    angles = v['angles']
    vel = v['vel']
    if not isinstance(links, list) or not links or any(L <= 0 for L in links):
        raise MechError('links: give positive link lengths [L1, ...] in m')
    if not isinstance(angles, list) or len(angles) != len(links):
        raise MechError('angles: give one joint angle (rad) per link')
    if not isinstance(vel, list) or len(vel) != 2:
        raise MechError('vel: give [vx, vy] in m/s')
    angles = [float(a) for a in angles]
    x, y = _fk_planar(links, angles)
    J = _jacobian_planar(links, angles)
    vv = np.array([float(vel[0]), float(vel[1])])
    theta_dot = np.linalg.pinv(J) @ vv  # min-norm solution of J theta_dot = v
    residual = float(np.hypot(*(J @ theta_dot - vv)))
    det = float(np.linalg.det(J)) if J.shape == (2, 2) else float(np.linalg.det(J @ J.T))
    sv = np.linalg.svd(J, compute_uv=False)
    warnings = []
    if sv[-1] < 1e-6 * sv[0]:
        warnings.append(f'Jacobian is (near-)singular (smallest singular value {sv[-1]:.3g} vs largest '
                        f'{sv[0]:.3g}); the min-norm joint velocity may not reproduce the requested tip '
                        f'velocity — see the residual')
    return {'position': [x, y], 'jacobian': J.tolist(), 'joint_vel': theta_dot.tolist(), 'det': det,
            'residual': residual, '_warnings': warnings}

assumptions: Geometric (basic) Jacobian J = [∂x/∂θ; ∂y/∂θ]. joint_vel is the minimum-norm least-squares solution of J θ̇ = v. At a singularity the pseudo-inverse still returns a finite (min-norm) answer, but it cannot reproduce an arbitrary tip velocity — the residual ‖J θ̇ − v‖ reports the shortfall and a warning is raised.
method_references: Geometric Jacobian of a planar arm; J θ̇ = v

robotics.planar_2r_dynamics.title: Planar 2R arm joint torques (closed-form Lagrange dynamics)

variables.name: lc1
variables.desc: distance from joint 1 to link-1 CoM

variables.name: lc2
variables.desc: distance from joint 2 to link-2 CoM

procedure.python:
def _planar_2r_dynamics(v):
    """Closed-form Lagrange/Newton–Euler torques of a planar 2R arm (relative joint angles, gravity −y).

    θ1 is the joint-1 angle from +x; θ2 is the joint-2 angle RELATIVE to link 1 (not absolute), so the
    inertia-matrix coupling term carries cos θ2. Gravity acts along −y.
    """
    L1, m1, m2 = v['L1'], v['m1'], v['m2']
    lc1, lc2, I1, I2 = v['lc1'], v['lc2'], v['I1'], v['I2']
    th1, th2 = v['theta1'], v['theta2']
    qd1, qd2, qdd1, qdd2 = v['qd1'], v['qd2'], v['qdd1'], v['qdd2']
    g = v['g']
    if min(L1, m1, m2, lc1, lc2) <= 0 or I1 < 0 or I2 < 0:
        raise MechError('lengths, masses and CoM distances must be positive; inertias non-negative')
    c2, s2 = math.cos(th2), math.sin(th2)
    c1, c12 = math.cos(th1), math.cos(th1 + th2)
    M11 = m1 * lc1 ** 2 + I1 + m2 * (L1 ** 2 + lc2 ** 2 + 2.0 * L1 * lc2 * c2) + I2
    M12 = m2 * (lc2 ** 2 + L1 * lc2 * c2) + I2
    M22 = m2 * lc2 ** 2 + I2
    # Christoffel-symbol Coriolis/centrifugal terms (h = -m2 L1 lc2 sin th2).
    tau1 = M11 * qdd1 + M12 * qdd2 - m2 * L1 * lc2 * s2 * (2.0 * qd1 * qd2 + qd2 ** 2) \
        + (m1 * lc1 + m2 * L1) * g * c1 + m2 * lc2 * g * c12
    tau2 = M12 * qdd1 + M22 * qdd2 + m2 * L1 * lc2 * s2 * qd1 ** 2 + m2 * lc2 * g * c12
    return {'tau1': tau1, 'tau2': tau2}

assumptions: Rigid links, revolute joints, gravity along −y. θ1 is measured from +x and θ2 is the joint-2 angle RELATIVE to link 1 (the relative-angle Lagrangian derivation), so the inertia coupling carries cos θ2; the link-2 CoM enters only through lc2 (no tip mass). Inertia matrix M(q), Coriolis/centrifugal and gravity terms from the standard Lagrangian derivation.
method_references: Lagrangian dynamics of a planar 2R manipulator (inertia, Coriolis and gravity terms)

robotics.payload_capacity.title: Static payload capacity of a planar 2R arm

variables.name: m_payload_max
variables.desc: maximum payload mass at the tip

variables.name: tau1_link
variables.desc: gravity torque of the links alone about joint 1

variables.name: tau2_link
variables.desc: gravity torque of the links alone about joint 2

procedure.python:
def _payload_capacity(v):
    """Static payload capacity of a planar 2R arm (links as point masses at mid-length, gravity −y).

    The payload sits at the tip. Each joint limits the payload through |τ_link + m·g·arm| ≤ τ_max, solved exactly
    for either sign of the link torque and moment arm (feasible interval clipped at m ≥ 0; capacity = upper end). A joint whose payload arm is ≈ 0
    (payload directly above/below it) imposes no static limit and is skipped with a warning.
    """
    L1, L2, th1, th2 = v['L1'], v['L2'], v['theta1'], v['theta2']
    m1, m2, g = v['m1'], v['m2'], v['g']
    tau1_max, tau2_max = v['tau1_max'], v['tau2_max']
    if min(L1, L2, m1, m2) <= 0 or g <= 0:
        raise MechError('lengths, masses and gravity must be positive')
    if tau1_max < 0 or tau2_max < 0:
        raise MechError('torque limits must be non-negative')
    c1, c12 = math.cos(th1), math.cos(th1 + th2)
    arm1 = L1 * c1 + L2 * c12          # signed payload moment arm about joint 1
    arm2 = L2 * c12                    # signed payload moment arm about joint 2
    tau1_link = m1 * g * (L1 / 2.0) * c1 + m2 * g * (L1 * c1 + (L2 / 2.0) * c12)  # signed holding torque
    tau2_link = m2 * g * (L2 / 2.0) * c12
    eps = 1e-9 * (L1 + L2)
    warnings = []

    def joint_range(j, tau_max, tau_link, arm):
        """Feasible payload interval for one joint from |τ_link + m·g·arm| ≤ τ_max (exact for either sign).

        The two bounds (±τ_max − τ_link)/(g·arm) bracket the feasible m; clip below at 0. Returns the upper
        end (capacity) or None when the arm is ≈ 0.
        """
        if abs(arm) < eps:
            warnings.append(f'joint {j}: payload moment arm ≈ 0 — the payload is not statically limited by joint {j}')
            return None
        b = sorted([(tau_max - tau_link) / (g * arm), (-tau_max - tau_link) / (g * arm)])
        lo, hi = max(0.0, b[0]), b[1]
        if hi < lo:
            raise MechError(f'no payload satisfies the joint-{j} torque limit in this pose')
        if lo > 0.0:
            warnings.append(f'joint {j}: the links alone exceed the torque limit; a payload of at least '
                            f'{lo:.6g} kg is needed to balance them')
        return hi

    m_cap_1 = joint_range(1, tau1_max, tau1_link, arm1)
    m_cap_2 = joint_range(2, tau2_max, tau2_link, arm2)
    caps = [c for c in (m_cap_1, m_cap_2) if c is not None]
    if not caps:
        raise MechError('the payload sits directly above the base (both moment arms ≈ 0): no static torque '
                        'limits the payload here')
    return {'m_payload_max': min(caps), 'm_cap_1': m_cap_1, 'm_cap_2': m_cap_2,
            'tau1_link': tau1_link, 'tau2_link': tau2_link, '_warnings': warnings}

assumptions: Static (no acceleration); links modelled as point masses at mid-length; gravity −y. Each joint limits the payload through |τ_link + m·g·arm| ≤ τ_max, using magnitudes so poses reaching either side of a joint are handled. A joint with payload moment arm ≈ 0 does not limit the payload. Payload sits at the tip.
method_references: Static joint-torque limit on the payload (min over joints)

robotics.trajectory_cubic.title: Cubic (rest-to-rest or via) joint trajectory polynomial
assumptions: Four boundary conditions (position and velocity at t = 0 and t = T). q is a generic coordinate (joint angle, displacement …), so position is unit-agnostic and velocity/acceleration are per-second. Acceleration is piecewise linear, so the rest-to-rest profile peaks at the ends. T must be positive; evaluating at t > T warns.

robotics.trajectory_quintic.title: Quintic joint trajectory polynomial (position, velocity and acceleration)
assumptions: Six boundary conditions (position, velocity and acceleration at both ends), so acceleration is continuous — no jerk spike at the endpoints. q is a generic coordinate, so position is unit-agnostic and velocity/acceleration are per-second. T must be positive; evaluating at t > T warns.

source.derivation: R=1, R=1, P=1, S=3 freedoms -> total 6; four joints
Standard DH with alpha=0 is a planar arm: x = 0.5 cos30 + 0.3 cos90 = 0.433013; y = 0.5 sin30 + 0.3 sin90 = 0.25 + 0.3 = 0.55; z = 0; two joints
Modified (Craig) DH T = Rot_x(30)Trans_x(0.5)Rot_z(45)Trans_z(0.3): translation is [a, -d sin(alpha), d cos(alpha)] = [0.5, -0.3 x 0.5, 0.3 x 0.866025] = [0.5, -0.15, 0.259808]

c2 = (0.25+0.16-0.25-0.16)/(2x0.5x0.4) = 0 -> theta2 = acos(0) = 90 deg (elbow-DOWN branch, theta2 > 0). Link 1 lies along +x so theta1 = atan2(0.4,0.5) - atan2(0.4, 0.5) = 0. Elbow-up branch: theta2_b = -90 deg; theta1_b = atan2(0.4,0.5) - atan2(-0.4,0.5) = 0.67474 + 0.67474 = 1.34948 rad

c2 = 0 -> theta2 = +/-90 deg. Elbow-down branch theta2=+90: theta1 = atan2(0.5,0.5) - atan2(0.5, 0.5) = 0, elbow at (L1 cos0, L1 sin0) = (0.5, 0) BELOW the base-tip line y=x. Elbow-up branch theta2=-90: theta1 = 45 - atan2(-0.5,0.5) = 45 - (-45) = 90 deg, elbow at (0.5 cos90, 0.5 sin90) = (0, 0.5) ABOVE the line
Target at the outer workspace boundary (r = L1 + L2 = 0.9): c2 = 1 -> acos(1) = 0, both branches coincide at the straight pose theta1 = theta2 = 0

phi = 90 deg so the wrist point is (0.5 - 0.5 cos90, 0.5 - 0.5 sin90) = (0.5, 0). 2R solve of (0.5,0) with L1=L2=0.5: c2 = (0.25 - 0.25 - 0.25)/0.5 = -0.5 -> theta2 = 120 deg; theta1 = 0 - atan2(0.4330, 0.25) = -60 deg; theta3 = 90 - (-60) - 120 = 30 deg. Branch b mirrors theta1=60, theta2=-120, theta3=150 deg
A converged IK must put the tip on the target: position = [0.3, 0.3] and tip-to-target error < 1e-6. Independent check of the solver, not the angles

theta2 = 0 puts the arm at a singularity (fully extended): the two Jacobian columns are both perpendicular to the arm (ratio 0.4/0.9), so det = 0 and the tip can only move perpendicular to the arm (direction 120 deg). The requested velocity [0, 1] = up has a component along the arm (30 deg) of |v| sin(30 deg) = 0.5 that cannot be produced at full extension; that radial component is the residual ||J qd - v|| = 0.5 m/s

Static horizontal pose (theta1=theta2=0, no motion, relative angles): gravity torque about each joint = g x (sum of mass x horizontal moment arm). tau1 = 9.80665(1x0.5 + 1x1.5) = 19.6133 N m; tau2 = 9.80665 x 1 x 0.5 = 4.90333 N m

Static torques with RELATIVE theta2=30 deg (link 2 absolute = 60 deg): link-1 CoM at x = lc1 cos30 = 0.433013, link-2 CoM at x = L1 cos30 + lc2 cos60 = 0.866025 + 0.25 = 1.116025. tau1 = g(m1 lc1 cos30 + m2 (L1 cos30 + lc2 cos60)) = 9.80665(0.433013 + 1.116025) = 9.80665 x 1.549038 = 15.1909; tau2 = g m2 lc2 cos60 = 9.80665 x 0.25 = 2.45166 (an absolute-angle theta2 would give a different value, so this pins the relative convention)
Rest-to-rest cubic q = 3t^2 - 2t^3 over T=1: q(0.5) = 0.75 - 0.25 = 0.5; qd = 6t - 6t^2 = 3 - 1.5 = 1.5; qdd = 6 - 12t = 0 (coordinate is unit-agnostic, so plain numbers)
Same rest-to-rest quintic scaled to T=2: q(t) = f(t/2) with f(u) = 10u^3 - 15u^4 + 6u^5. At t=1 (u=0.5): q = 0.5; qd = f'(0.5)/2 = 1.875/2 = 0.9375; qdd = f''(0.5)/4 = 0
